Net book value × depreciation percentage rate. Depreciation is higher in early years and falls each year.
Cost of a non-current asset minus accumulated (provision for) depreciation.

body.back: An expense incurred in the period but not yet paid at the year end. Added to the expense; shown as a current liability.
An expense paid in advance for the next period. Deducted from the expense; shown as a current asset.
Income received in the period that relates to a future period. Deducted from income; shown as a current liability.
body.front: What is income received in advance?

body.back: Income earned in the period but not yet received at the year end. Added to income; shown as a current asset.
A debt that a customer cannot pay. It is written off as an expense in the income statement and removed from trade receivables.
body.front: What is an irrecoverable debt (bad debt)?

body.back: An estimate of trade receivables that may become irrecoverable in future, usually a percentage of trade receivables after deducting bad debts written off.
body.front: What is a provision for doubtful debts?

body.back: An increase is an expense in the income statement; a decrease is added to profit (income). Only the change is recorded.
body.front: How is a change in the provision for doubtful debts treated?

body.back: Deducted from trade receivables in current assets.
body.front: Where is the provision for doubtful debts shown in the statement of financial position?

body.back: To follow the accruals (matching) concept: income and expenses are matched to the period in which they occur, not when cash is paid or received.
body.front: Why are adjustments made at the year end?

body.back: Expense increases, so profit for the year decreases. Current liabilities increase.
